sentence_stem: Not until the last chapter was finished
correct_completion: did the author reveal the murderer's identity.
full_sentence: Not until the last chapter was finished did the author reveal the murderer's identity.
acceptable_variants: did the novelist finally name the killer.
did the writer at last disclose who the murderer was.

options.text: the author finally revealed the murderer's identity.
options.why_wrong: After 'not until', English requires subject-auxiliary inversion, so 'did the author' must follow. This statement keeps the normal word order and is ungrammatical here.

options.text: the final chapter was very long.
options.why_wrong: This adds a description but does not provide the inverted main clause that 'not until' requires.

options.text: did the author finally reveal the murderer's identity.
the reader had already guessed the ending.
options.why_wrong: This is a plain statement with normal word order, so it does not fit the inversion needed after 'not until'.

grammar_focus: Subject-auxiliary inversion after the negative time expression 'not until'
explanation: When a sentence begins with 'not until' followed by a clause, the main clause must use inverted word order with an auxiliary verb. Learners should check that the auxiliary comes before the subject in the main clause.
